derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, regulation, recognised industry body or explicit judgment. No client or product practice is generalised.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: The Source Authority Pack names no wildfire deenergization or public-safety shutoff authority. It supplies no criteria, approval route, notice requirement, patrol method, restoration threshold, evidence package or retention rule for 9.6; those fields are marked judgment.

The Source Authority Pack refers generically to Edison Electric Institute mutual assistance and business continuity but gives no document title, edition, locator or process standard. Organisation, mobilisation, logistics, onboarding and demobilisation details in 9.4 are therefore judgment except where a regulation or GFMAM applies.

No permitted source states a restoration-effort calculation, estimated-time-to-restore method, confidence scale, refresh cadence or cross-commodity restoration-ranking rule. Processes 9.2.3, 9.2.4 and 9.3.1 are SPEC because a Decision Model and Notation (DMN) model would invent those rules.

IEEE 1366-2022 and IEEE 1782-2022 are named in the pack without clause locators. They are cited at consensus where only the published standard and subject are claimed; no paywalled body text is paraphrased.
IEC 61968 work, message and component vocabulary is electric-scoped. Gas emergency work has no equivalent work-item information model and borrows the electric vocabulary here.
IEC 61968-6 cl. 4.2 has no document-management or emergency-management component. Emergency plans and evidence are placed on MAI, and the namespace gap is not filled with an invented code.
GFMAM Landscape subject 3.9 Contingency Planning and Resilience Analysis is only partial: 9.4 and 9.6 cover response, but the model has no pre-event resilience-analysis process.

APQC 14.1.8 activity 19302 places media and public relations inside emergency response. This model puts general outage notice at 10.3.3 but keeps wildfire notice at 9.6.2; the cross-category boundary warrants review.

Neither APQC 14.1.8 nor GFMAM subject 6.6 supplies a wildfire-specific process group. Group 9.6 repeats planning, execution, restoration and cost-evidence functions also present in 9.4, 9.3 and 10.3; whether it is a process group or an event-type overlay warrants review.
EN 17007 has no direct process for emergency organisation, outage forecasting, mutual assistance or emergency network switching. The closest level-2 mappings are used and the mismatch is not hidden.

merge_corrections.what: 24 entries in `sources` justified the NOTATION rather than the process content - 15 x 'EN 17007 Table 2, BPMN 2.0 notation' and 9 x 'Campaign notation selection rule applied to this process instance'. Neither says anything about the process it sits on, the second cites this campaign's own prompt, and `notation.why` already carries the rationale. No other merged category does this. Removed; every process still carries three or more citations of its own content, so nothing was propping up the minimum.

Four processes composed a header band longer than its three-line box - 9.1.1, 9.3.2, 9.6.2 and 9.6.3, the longest at 498 characters against a 477 cap. Every individual length was inside its own budget; the budget never covered the COMPOSED string the slide actually renders. Trigger text and two activities tightened on each, meaning unchanged. content_budget.block_total.header_band now carries the cap and validate_spec.py enforces it.
